title: Trump: New York investigates Ivanka and Don Jr. for Trump SoHo scheme
description_short: Trump: New York investigates Ivanka and Don Jr. for Trump SoHo scheme
description_medium: TrumpFile.org reports that New York investigators examined Ivanka Trump and Donald Trump Jr.’s marketing of Trump SoHo units, alleging that sales figures were inflated to attract buyers. The account cites emails about sales claims; it also says attorneys argued that exaggerating value was not a crime and the inquiry later ended without charges.
description_long: TrumpFile.org’s timeline says New York’s Major Economic Crimes Bureau opened an inquiry in 2010 into how Ivanka Trump and Donald Trump Jr. marketed units at the Trump SoHo hotel and condominium project. The article reports that investigators examined claims that sales figures were inflated to attract prospective buyers and describes emails that, according to people who had seen them, showed the siblings discussing those figures. It also reports that Trump Organization lawyers argued the exaggerations were not criminal. The inquiry continued for about two years and was eventually dropped, according to the linked page. The supplied source does not include the underlying emails, an indictment, or a court finding that the siblings committed fraud. The account is therefore an allegation about a real-estate marketing investigation and its closure, not a finding of guilt. A fuller account would require the investigative record and the decision explaining why prosecutors closed the matter.

title: Federal Ban on LGBTQ+ Content in Media and Schools - Expression Criminalization and Censorship
description_short: Federal Ban on LGBTQ+ Content in Media and Schools - Expression Criminalization and Censorship
description_long: Donald Trump implemented comprehensive federal bans on LGBTQ+ content in media and schools by classifying any acknowledgment of LGBTQ+ existence as 'pornography' while criminalizing educators, librarians, and media producers who created content that recognized sexual orientation or gender identity diversity through Project 2025's systematic censorship and expression elimination. The systematic content prohibition represented Trump's transformation of LGBTQ+ acknowledgment from protected speech into criminal activity, requiring teachers and librarians to register as sex offenders for sharing materials that discussed LGBTQ+ topics while eliminating federal funding for any educational institution that maintained inclusive content or programming. The LGBTQ+ censorship included eliminating media coverage, educational materials, library books, and online content that acknowledged LGBTQ+ existence while establishing federal monitoring systems that identified and prosecuted violations of content bans through surveillance and reporting mechanisms that enabled systematic persecution of LGBTQ+ expression. Trump's content criminalization violated First Amendment protections for free speech and expression by treating LGBTQ+ acknowledgment as obscenity while using federal power to eliminate diverse perspectives and inclusive content from public discourse, education, and media representation. The expression ban created what civil rights advocates called 'systematic erasure' of LGBTQ+ Americans through content prohibition that eliminated visibility, representation, and educational resources while forcing LGBTQ+ individuals into invisibility and isolation through comprehensive censorship of their existence and experiences. The LGBTQ+ content elimination represented Project 2025's vision of media and education controlled by heteronormative ideology rather than diverse representation, transforming inclusive content from protected expression into criminal activity while eliminating LGBTQ+ voices and perspectives from public discourse through systematic censorship and expression criminalization.
subcategory: LGBTQ+ Content Prohibition and Expression Criminalization

title: Trump: Epstein consults Ken Starr to protect Trump
description_short: Trump: Epstein consults Ken Starr to protect Trump
description_medium: TrumpFile.org reports that emails released by the House Oversight Committee showed Jeffrey Epstein telling an associate that he had spoken with Ken Starr in August 2018, after Michael Cohen pleaded guilty in the Trump campaign-finance matter. The page says the discussion concerned a possible Trump response; it does not establish that Starr agreed to act for Trump.
description_long: TrumpFile.org reports that emails released by the House Oversight Committee in November 2025 included a message from Jeffrey Epstein describing a conversation with attorney Ken Starr on August 22, 2018. The exchange came after Michael Cohen pleaded guilty to campaign-finance violations connected to the Trump campaign. The page says Epstein and Starr discussed a strategy Trump might use to avoid consequences for hush-money payments, and notes that Starr later joined Trump’s Senate impeachment defense team in 2020. The linked account does not provide a transcript of the conversation or show that Starr accepted a request to represent Trump in 2018. It also does not establish that the discussion changed any legal proceeding. The entry records the reported timing and subject of the email, while leaving the full conversation and its practical effect unresolved. The source is evidence of Epstein’s account of a conversation, not proof of an agreement or outcome.

title: Trump: White House official involved in Ukraine scandal is promoted to the NSA
description_short: Trump: White House official involved in Ukraine scandal is promoted to the NSA
description_medium: TrumpFile.org reports that the Pentagon named Michael Ellis, a former lawyer for Representative Devin Nunes and a National Security Council official, as the NSA’s top lawyer on November 9, 2020. The article says the White House pressed for the appointment and links Ellis to earlier disputes over classified material and the Ukraine inquiry.
description_long: On November 9, 2020, the Pentagon named Michael Ellis as general counsel of the National Security Agency, according to TrumpFile.org’s timeline. Ellis had served as counsel to Representative Devin Nunes and then worked on the National Security Council staff. The article reports that the White House pushed for his appointment and describes Ellis’s earlier role in preparing classified material that Nunes used to support claims of surveillance by the Obama administration. Those claims later unraveled, and Nunes recused himself from the House Russia investigation. The timing placed the appointment in the post-election transition, when Trump remained president and senior national-security positions were still being filled. The supplied account links Ellis’s prior work to the Ukraine controversy, but it does not establish that his appointment changed NSA operations or that he misused classified information in the new role. The entry documents the promotion and the background reported about the official, leaving its operational consequences unspecified.

title: Trump: J.D. Vance wants to track women seeking abortions
description_short: Trump: J.D. Vance wants to track women seeking abortions
description_medium: In June 2023, Senator J.D. Vance and other lawmakers urged HHS Secretary Xavier Becerra to oppose a Biden administration rule limiting law-enforcement access to reproductive-health records. Their letter argued that the rule impeded enforcement of state abortion laws. It records a request to weaken privacy protections, not an implemented pregnancy-tracking system, and the supplied account does not document a direct Trump proposal.
description_long: Senator J.D. Vance and other conservative lawmakers wrote to Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra on June 16, 2023, objecting to a Biden administration rule that restricted law-enforcement access to reproductive-health records. Their letter argued that the rule exceeded HHS authority and impeded enforcement of state abortion laws. The linked account says the rule covered records related to reproductive care, including fertility treatment, contraception and miscarriage, and limited disclosure for investigations into legally provided care. The lawmakers asked the department to undo that privacy protection; their letter did not create a pregnancy-monitoring system. The headline characterizes their position as wanting to track women seeking abortions, but the supplied material identifies no tracking database or implementation. It also mentions Trump’s support for abortion surveillance without a direct quotation or policy details. The 2023 letter documents Vance’s position; a Trump-specific proposal and any actual tracking system would require separate evidence.
organization_tags: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

title: Vance Guest-Hosted Charlie Kirk Show and Urged Listeners to Report Kirk Critics
description_short: After Kirk’s killing, Vance guest-hosted his show and urged listeners to report people celebrating it to their employers, according to the Guardian.
description_medium: The linked Guardian report says Vice President JD Vance guest-hosted The Charlie Kirk Show after Charlie Kirk’s killing and urged listeners to identify people celebrating his death and report them to their employers. That account documents a call to expose and pressure critics; it does not support the title’s description of the episode as being held in Kirk’s honor. The supplied record contains no separate source for that claim.
description_long: The supplied Guardian article concerns Vice President JD Vance guest-hosting The Charlie Kirk Show after Kirk was killed. In the report, Vance urged listeners to identify people celebrating Kirk’s death and contact their employers, a call the article characterized as a doxing campaign. The account therefore supports describing the episode as a public appeal to expose and pressure critics of Kirk, rather than as a program simply held in Kirk’s honor. It does not provide a transcript of the full episode or establish how many people were identified, reported, or affected. The record’s title frames the event differently, and no second source is supplied to explain whether it refers to another broadcast or to the same appearance. A reader-facing account can state what the Guardian reported, but the title and event description need reconciliation before this record can be treated as a fully verified account of the titled event. A transcript or contemporaneous source for the specific episode would establish its date, framing, and full remarks.

description_short: Trump: J.D. Vance has Epstein file strategy meeting with other Trump officials, insists that it never happened
description_medium: TrumpFile.org reports that Vice President J.D. Vance, Attorney General Pam Bondi, and FBI Director Kash Patel met on August 6, 2025, to discuss how the administration would handle the Jeffrey Epstein files. The page says Vance’s team denied the meeting, while the article describes specific topics reportedly discussed.
description_long: TrumpFile.org reports that Vice President J.D. Vance, Attorney General Pam Bondi, and FBI Director Kash Patel met at the White House on August 6, 2025, to discuss the administration’s handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files. The article says the meeting aimed to align public messaging and may also have addressed tensions between Bondi and Patel. It reports that the possible release of Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche’s interview with Ghislaine Maxwell was discussed, while Vance and his staff denied that the meeting occurred. The page says the report it relied on named specific topics, but the supplied packet does not include minutes, an attendee list, or an official record confirming the conversation. It also offers speculation about why other officials were absent; this entry does not treat that speculation as established fact. The account documents a reported meeting and a denial, leaving the full participant list and discussion unverified.
